facts.label: Purchase price
facts.detail: The sum the United States agreed to pay Russia for Alaska in 1867.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Treaty signed
facts.detail: Signed in Washington by US Secretary of State William Seward and Russian minister Eduard de Stoeckl, at 4 a.m. after negotiating through the night.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Senate vote
facts.detail: The US Senate ratified the treaty on April 9, 1867.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Formal handover
facts.detail: In Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag was raised.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Price per acre
facts.detail: Roughly 1,518,800 km² (375 million acres) for $7.2 million works out to about 1.9 cents an acre.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Size compared with France
facts.detail: Alaska has about 1,481,346 km² of land, against about 543,940 km² for metropolitan France.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.label: Prudhoe Bay oil discovery
facts.detail: Prudhoe Bay is the largest oil field in the United States.
facts.videoTitle: Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre

facts.detail: Drawn by Gerardus Mercator for navigators; it enlarges areas about 4 times at 60° latitude and about 10.5 times at 72°.
